conclusion: Confirmed a process-global cross-session state leak: pool.xedge_focus is written by d6_multiref_wm_production_organ.py (always CAND_POOLS[0], a positional constant) whenever ANY session's turn holds >=2 referents, and is NEVER cleared by any live code path. Session A held 2 referents through the real production call and its own ambiguous transitive read role=agent/wm_resolved=true/wm_margin=0.020 (content_role=patient) -- lesion-attributable (lesioning the cross-edge reverted role to patient, wm_resolved absent). Session C -- a brand-new organ instance whose own referent codebook was confirmed empty, i.e. it never held anything -- was given the IDENTICAL ambiguous sentence and read role=agent/wm_resolved=true/wm_margin=0.018, indistinguishable from session A's own result, purely because session A's unrelated hold happened earlier in the SAME process. The mechanism itself (cross-edge learning + lesion-attributable role drive) is real and reproduced here through the real production call path; what fails is the real wiring's session isolation, never exercised by the finding's own self-test (which manually assigns xedge_focus rather than driving it through d6org.judge/.load). This blocks the default-flip under the moat-safe / no-cross-session-bleed bar. A secondary, UNRELATED-to-xedge observation surfaced in passing: the well-formed control sentence read comprehended=false on a truly fresh, xedge-never-imported standalone organ at seed 42 (margin 0.038 vs threshold 0.249) -- a pre-existing property of this organ's own calibration on this sentence, not caused by xedge, left as an open item.
